title: validate
description: Format validation behavior of Triauth.validate({identifier?, deviceName?}). validate is synchronous and pure - it touches no DNS, clock, or randomness - so dnsEntries/currentTime are present only for schema parity and are ignored. These cases alone exercise every reachable branch of validate() (validation.js. NOTE: the null/non-object/array early-return inside hasOnlyKnownProperties is unreachable from validate (the code invalid_arguments guard rejects those inputs first), and the 'whitelisted-key-with-undefined-value' rejection inside it is not expressible in JSON (JSON has no undefined); both are therefore intentionally uncovered by this JSON suite.

tests.name: ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: no argument at all (objects === undefined) -> falsy operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: explicit null argument -> falsy operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: string argument -> typeof !== 'object' operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: number argument -> typeof !== 'object' operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: array argument -> Array.isArray operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: empty object -> Object.keys(objects).length === 0 operand
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: unrecognized key -> hasOnlyKnownProperties .every returns false
ARG GUARD invalid_arguments: an otherwise valid identifier plus a stray key is still rejected
CONFIG GUARD invalid_config: a misspelled config override key is rejected in validate's {valid,errors} shape (merged-config validation, mirrors the rest of the API)
CONFIG GUARD invalid_config: a valid config override is accepted and object validation proceeds (valid identifier -> valid:true)
CONFIG GUARD invalid_config: the objects guard takes precedence - a bad objects key returns invalid_arguments even when config is also misspelled

tests.name: IDENTIFIER valid: exactly 120 bytes (identifierBytesize) passes - the byteSize check is strict-greater, pinning the boundary against off-by-one ports
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/too_long: one byte over identifierBytesize (121 > 120) is rejected - the boundary-negative twin of the 120-byte positive
IDENTIFIER valid: name-part at exactly 63 characters (the grammar cap: alnum *62) passes
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_username: name-part of 64 characters exceeds the 63-character grammar cap (alnum *62) while staying under the identifierBytesize total
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_username: a plus sign in the username (john+work) is rejected - '+' is not a username character
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid: embedded NUL (U+0000) is rejected by the same whitespace-and-NUL check, not the grammar
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_domain: IPv4-literal domain (john@1.2.3.4) - a numeric final label is never a domain part
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_domain: all-digits final label (john@example.99) - real TLDs are never numeric
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_domain: 0x-hex final label (john@example.0xff) - exotic IPv4 spellings fall to the same numeric-final-label rule
IDENTIFIER valid: domain label at exactly 63 characters (the DNS label cap) passes
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_domain: domain label of 64 characters exceeds the 63-character DNS label cap while staying under the identifierBytesize total
IDENTIFIER invalid_identifier/invalid_domain: single-character final label (john@a.b) - a final label is at least two characters
DEVICENAME valid: exactly 20 bytes (the cap) passes - strict-greater check, boundary companion of the invalid_device_name/too_long case
